newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory 96/97 coffee bean exports slump year-on.
newsitem.headline: Ivory 96/97 coffee bean exports slump year-on.

text.p: Ivory Coast exported 1,247 tonnes of robusta coffee beans in December 1996/97 against 3,550 tonnes in November and 6,159 tonnes in December 1995, official shipping data show.
Shipments included 961 tonnes of beans leaving from Abidjan, against 1,932 and 286 tonnes from San Pedro, the second port, against 1,618 for the same period last year.
No roasted coffee was shipped but 498 tonnes of soluble coffee left Abidjan, against 765 tonnes in November.
Cumulative coffee bean exports from October 1 1996 to December 31 were 12,827 tonnes against 20,081 tonnes in the same period of 1995/96.
Coffee exports were slower in early 1996/97 because of a combination of unfavourable world demand, low prices and bankers' caution over export financing.
World robusta prices rose after an international export limitation agreement in January.
Ivorian exporters expect volumes to rise from this month.
Ivory Coast's coffee season traditionally opens at the same time as the cocoa season in early October.
Coffee marketing usually picks up along with exports in late January after peak cocoa marketing.
